{"findings": [
  {
    "file": "app/models/optimized_image.rb",
    "line": 149,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "api",
    "title": "Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height overload",
    "body": "The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: the pre-existing `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and the newly added `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the four-argument form quietly disappears. Existing callers using `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` will bind `height` to `opts`, and `optimize` later evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer, raising NoMethodError; callers passing five arguments raise ArgumentError. This is a public class-method contract break and will also break any existing specs. Remove or rename one overload (or dispatch on argument count) and update callers."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 66,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Downsize loop ignores failures and proceeds with an oversized or corrupt file",
    "body": "`OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when the ImageMagick/gifsicle command fails or the output cannot be written, but the loop ignores the return value and merely decrements `attempt`. After five failures it exits and `Upload.create_for` is called with the original tempfile, so an image still larger than `max_image_size_kb` (or a partially written file) can be persisted as an upload, with no error returned to the user. There is also no final size check after the loop. Check the downsize result/final size and reject with a clear error instead of silently storing the oversized file."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js",
    "line": 182,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores per-type site settings",
    "body": "Both client-side checks were changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (and `max_image_size_kb` in the 413 handler at line 246) to a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. This raises the client-side limit for attachments to 10MB regardless of `max_attachment_size_kb`, so files the admin disallowed pass validation and are sent to the server. For images, an admin who configures `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB now sees valid uploads rejected, while an unlimited (0) setting is effectively capped at 10MB. The 10MB constant is duplicated in the 413 handler, so the two can drift. Use the site setting, or `max(setting, 10MB)` only for images, and share a single constant."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 55,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "api",
    "title": "API download cap hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring configured limits",
    "body": "`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the configured limit with a fixed 10MB. If `max_image_size_kb` or the attachment limit is configured higher than 10MB, permitted API uploads now fail; if configured lower, the server will download and store files larger than the site's limit (non-images are never downsized). The same 10MB value is also duplicated in the JavaScript client, so client and server limits can silently diverge. Derive the download limit from the relevant site setting, with the 10MB floor only if that is the intended behavior for images."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 67,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Animated GIF downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle",
    "body": "This call passes dimensions `\"80%\"` together with `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. When `optimize` selects the animated path (for a `from` path ending in `.GIF`), `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which builds `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80% ...`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects a `WxH` value, not a percentage, so the command fails, the loop burns all five attempts, and the oversized GIF is uploaded unchanged. If the temp path does not end in `.GIF`, the animated branch is not selected at all. Pass pixel dimensions (or use the percentage only with `convert`), and ensure the animated path is actually selected for browser uploads."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 64,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "test_gap",
    "title": "No tests for the new auto-downsize behavior",
    "body": "The PR adds non-trivial branching (image vs non-image, successful downsize, downsize failure, animated GIFs, oversized files, API url uploads) without any specs. Tests exercising these paths would have caught the overridden `downsize` signature and the invalid `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` command. Add coverage for `create_upload` downsize behavior and the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions)` overload."
  }
]}

findings.title: Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height overload
findings.body: The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: the pre-existing `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and the newly added `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the four-argument form quietly disappears. Existing callers using `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` will bind `height` to `opts`, and `optimize` later evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer, raising NoMethodError; callers passing five arguments raise ArgumentError. This is a public class-method contract break and will also break any existing specs. Remove or rename one overload (or dispatch on argument count) and update callers.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failures and proceeds with an oversized or corrupt file
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` when the ImageMagick/gifsicle command fails or the output cannot be written, but the loop ignores the return value and merely decrements `attempt`. After five failures it exits and `Upload.create_for` is called with the original tempfile, so an image still larger than `max_image_size_kb` (or a partially written file) can be persisted as an upload, with no error returned to the user. There is also no final size check after the loop. Check the downsize result/final size and reject with a clear error instead of silently storing the oversized file.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores per-type site settings
findings.body: Both client-side checks were changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` (and `max_image_size_kb` in the 413 handler at line 246) to a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. This raises the client-side limit for attachments to 10MB regardless of `max_attachment_size_kb`, so files the admin disallowed pass validation and are sent to the server. For images, an admin who configures `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB now sees valid uploads rejected, while an unlimited (0) setting is effectively capped at 10MB. The 10MB constant is duplicated in the 413 handler, so the two can drift. Use the site setting, or `max(setting, 10MB)` only for images, and share a single constant.

findings.title: API download cap hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring configured limits
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the configured limit with a fixed 10MB. If `max_image_size_kb` or the attachment limit is configured higher than 10MB, permitted API uploads now fail; if configured lower, the server will download and store files larger than the site's limit (non-images are never downsized). The same 10MB value is also duplicated in the JavaScript client, so client and server limits can silently diverge. Derive the download limit from the relevant site setting, with the 10MB floor only if that is the intended behavior for images.

findings.title: Animated GIF downsize passes a percentage to gifsicle
findings.body: This call passes dimensions `"80%"` together with `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. When `optimize` selects the animated path (for a `from` path ending in `.GIF`), `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which builds `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80% ...`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects a `WxH` value, not a percentage, so the command fails, the loop burns all five attempts, and the oversized GIF is uploaded unchanged. If the temp path does not end in `.GIF`, the animated branch is not selected at all. Pass pixel dimensions (or use the percentage only with `convert`), and ensure the animated path is actually selected for browser uploads.

findings.title: No tests for the new auto-downsize behavior
findings.body: The PR adds non-trivial branching (image vs non-image, successful downsize, downsize failure, animated GIFs, oversized files, API url uploads) without any specs. Tests exercising these paths would have caught the overridden `downsize` signature and the invalid `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` command. Add coverage for `create_upload` downsize behavior and the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions)` overload.
